I didn't know about his existing relationship until he felt guilty enough to tell me. He said it was a one-time thing, but still, it hurt because I felt used and deceived. Then, a month ago, this cheating happened, and now, through a mutual coworker, I found out who the other girl is. But her response was really rude. She basically said they had already discussed it and that I should never contact her again. Now I'm feeling dumb for bringing it up since she said they were over it. I'm wondering if I should have just kept my mouth shut instead of trying to help. So, is it right or wrong for me to have told her about the cheating? Let me think about the different aspects of this situation. First, honesty. I believe in honesty, especially in relationships. If someone is cheating, it's important for the other person to know so they can make informed decisions. But in this case, I wasn't in a committed relationship with him; I was the side chick. Does that change things? Then, there's the aspect of respect for the other person's privacy and their relationship. Even though he cheated on her, she might have already dealt with it and moved on. By contacting her, I might have reopened old wounds or caused unnecessary stress. Also, there's the issue of how she responded. She was rude and told me not to contact her again. That makes me feel bad, especially since I thought I was doing the right thing. Maybe I overstepped by contacting her without knowing the full story or how she felt about it. On the other hand, I feel like I was trying to help her by letting her know what happened. I didn't want her to be in a relationship with someone who was dishonest. But maybe there's a better way to handle this situation without directly contacting her. I'm also thinking about the consequences of my actions. By sending her screenshots and telling her what happened, I might have damaged my reputation or made things awkward at work since we have a mutual coworker. Plus, it could have strained my relationship with him, even though he was the one who cheated. Another thing to consider is whether I had the right to contact her in the first place. I wasn't her friend or someone close to her; I was involved with her boyfriend. By contacting her, I might have overstepped boundaries and invaded her privacy. I'm also wondering about the emotional impact on me. I felt used and hurt when I found out about the cheating, and now I'm feeling guilty and dumb for reaching out to her. It's making me question my own judgment and whether I handled the situation appropriately. Maybe I should have talked to someone I trust about this instead of acting on my emotions. Talking to a friend or a counselor could have helped me process my feelings and decide the best way to handle it without directly contacting her. In the end, I'm trying to figure out if my actions were right or wrong. I wanted to do the right thing by letting her know about the cheating, but it backfired and made things worse. I'm not sure if I should have kept my mouth shut or if there was a better way to handle it. I think I need to reflect on the consequences of my actions and consider the perspectives of everyone involved. It's important to balance honesty with respect for others' privacy and to handle situations in a way that doesn't cause unnecessary harm.
